mekayis.metin:
(قَنَبَ) الْقَافُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى جَمْعٍ وَتَجَمُّعٍ. مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمِقْنَبُ: الْقِطْعَةُ مِنَ الْخَيْلِ، يُقَالُ هِيَ نَحْوُ الْأَرْبَعِينَ. وَالْقَنِيبُ: الْجَمَاعَةُ مِنَ النَّاسِ.
قَالَ ابْنُ دُرَيْدٍ: قَنَّبَ الزَّرْعُ تَقْنِيبًا، إِذَا أَعْصَفَ. قَالَ: وَتُسَمَّى الْعَصِيفَةُ: الْقُنَّابَةَ. وَالْعَصِيفَةُ: الْوَرَقُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ الَّذِي يَكُونُ فِيهِ السُّنْبُلُ.
وَمِنَ الْبَابِ: الْقُنْبُ، وَهُوَ وِعَاءُ ثِيلِ الْفَرَسِ، وَسُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ لِأَنَّهُ يَجْمَعُ مَا فِيهِ. وَأَمَّا الْقُنَّبُ فَزَعَمَ [قَوْمٌ] أَنَّهَا عَرَبِيَّةٌ. فَإِنْ كَانَ كَذَا فَهُوَ مِنْ قَنَبَ الزَّرْعُ، إِذَا أَعْصَفَ. وَهُوَ شَيْءٌ لَا يُتَّخَذُ مِنْ بَعْضِ ذَلِكَ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Aramaic, there being Jewish Babylonian Aramaic קִינְּבָא (qinnəḇā, “hemp”), Classical Syriac ܩܢܦܐ (qənappā, “hemp”), and other forms. See Ancient Greek κάνναβις (kánnabis, “hemp”) for related terms.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قُنْب • (qunb) m (plural قُنُوب (qunūb))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Probably from an Aramaic term cognate to Classical Syriac ܩܘܽܢܒܳܐ (qunbā, “greater sail of a ship”) in a more general meaning of a “sleeve, covering sheath or membrane”, possibly related to the mentioned word for hemp, relating to fabrics being made from hemp; hence “to enter or go into” and perhaps more via the idea of “going forth or around” also the names of military detachments.
s: Classical Syriac ܩܘܽܢܒܳܐ (qunbā, “greater sail of a ship”)
g: the membrane or sheath in which certain animals have the male member, particularly a lion
the prepuce of the clitoris of a human female
dr: قَنَّبَ; to form a squadron, to journey with collect men on horse”)
also called ذَنَب الْأَسَد and ذَيْل الْأَسَد
denoting the star Denebola in the constellation Leo

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Probably from an Aramaic term cognate to Classical Syriac ܩܘܽܢܒܳܐ (qunbā, “greater sail of a ship”) in a more general meaning of a “sleeve, covering sheath or membrane”, possibly related to the mentioned word for hemp, relating to fabrics being made from hemp; hence “to enter or go into” and perhaps more via the idea of “going forth or around” also the names of military detachments.
s: Classical Syriac ܩܘܽܢܒܳܐ (qunbā, “greater sail of a ship”)
g: to come out and forth from its involucrum
namely, into the house or tent
to withdraw the claw into the receptacle (said of a lion)

s: Classical Syriac ܩܘܽܢܒܳܐ (qunbā, “greater sail of a ship”)
g: to put forth the قُنَّابَة (qunnāba, “leaves in which an ear of grain is enveloped”)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قَنَبَ • (qanaba) I (non-past يَقْنِبُ (yaqnibu), verbal noun قَنْب (qanb))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Likely of ideophonic origin, as also known of German knappen, abknappen. A connection to the senses of the aforementioned root of entering into envelopes via the idea of putting the hand into vegetation is unlikely since plantations are pruned from the outside, especially with the kinds of growings relevant in the Arab world.
g: to prune, to cut off from (the object being a vine)
